# Jubilees Chapter 21 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 21:6 — "the fat is the glory" vs. "the fat belongs to God"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the fat is the glory" | Literal Ge'ez shebeḥ |
| LOGOS | "the fat is the glory" | Same — literal formula |
| PNEUMA | "the fat is the glory" | Same — retained as important formula |

**SOPHIA:** All three agree. "The fat is the glory" is the Jubilees rendering of the priestly formula. No disagreement here; logged for completeness.

---

## 21:11 — altar construction prohibition

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "not of stones hewn with iron, and not of hewed stone" | Double prohibition, literal |
| LOGOS | "not of stones cut by iron tools; do not build it of hewn stone" | Formal, slight restructuring |
| PNEUMA | "no iron tools, no shaped stones. Keep it natural" | Dynamic compression |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. The double prohibition is structurally important (cf. Exod 20:25; Deut 27:5); LOGOS preserves both elements cleanly. PNEUMA's "keep it natural" is overly casual. EMET's awkward double negative is preserved in LOGOS more elegantly.

---

## 21:16 — the wood list

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "cypress, and pine, and almond, and fir, and cedar, and juniper, and fig and olive and myrtle and laurel and aspalathus and balsam" | Full list with Ge'ez-influenced sequence |
| LOGOS | "cypress, pine, almond, fir, cedar, juniper, fig, olive, myrtle, laurel, aspalathus, and balsam" | Same species, standard punctuation |
| PNEUMA | Same list | Same species, no deviation |

**SOPHIA:** All three translators agree on the species list. The only divergence is punctuation (EMET uses "and" throughout per Ge'ez style; LOGOS/PNEUMA use commas). Adopted LOGOS punctuation as more readable. EMET's polysyndeton preserved in the disagreement log as notable.

---

## 21:19 — "guard yourself and your soul" vs. "guard yourself and your life"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "guard yourself and your soul from all blood" | Literal nafsa = soul |
| LOGOS | "guard yourself and your life from all blood" | "Life" for nafsa in this context |
| PNEUMA | "guard your life and keep away from blood" | Dynamic compression |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. In the context of blood prohibition, "life" is the operative meaning of nafsa here (blood = life). EMET's "soul" is technically accurate but misleading in modern English. PNEUMA loses the self-address structure.

---

## 21:26 — scope of what Abraham wrote

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "all the law and all the statutes and all the judgments" | Triple Ge'ez list |
| LOGOS | "the entire law, all the statutes, and all the ordinances" | Formal, "ordinances" for judgments |
| PNEUMA | "the entire law, all the statutes and ordinances" | Compressed to two elements |

**SOPHIA:** Adopted LOGOS. The tripartite formula (law/statutes/judgments) is structurally significant in Jubilees' legal vocabulary; PNEUMA's compression loses one element. "Ordinances" preferred over EMET's "judgments" as it better captures the legislative sense of the Ge'ez.

---

**Total disagreements: 5**
